item.statement: The authors attempted to replace Vanadium with Iron to create a low-activation alloy, but this approach failed due to the formation of undesired intermetallic phases and a lowered melting point.
quotes: However, the addition of Fe in both low and high elemental concentrations promotes the formation of several undesired intermetallic phases instead of single-phase solid-solution
as well as lowering the melting point of the system.
Due to failure of this approach, a quinary HEA was planned considering the principles introduced by the VEC model.

item.statement: The study acknowledges that the two film compositions tested were different due to deposition challenges, meaning the results for the thick film are inferred from the thin film rather than being identical.
quotes: We acknowledge that both films have different compositions, which is due to challenges in depositing specific compositions from five different targets within this quinary system.
However, it should be noted that different compositions, tested in thin film forms, led to similar single-phase BCC microstructures with similar irradiation responses
Hence, the thick film composition follows similar irradiation resistance.

item.statement: The authors identify that the high migration barrier of He-vacancy complexes, which may explain the absence of preferential bubble formation at grain boundaries, requires further investigation.
quotes: The absence of preferential bubble formation at grain boundaries can also stem from the high migration barrier of He-vacancy complexes, which still needs to be further investigated.
The contribution of grain boundaries, however, compared to grain matrices to the irradiation resistance has been studied comparing NC HEA and coarse grain HEA to NC-W and coarse grain W
and it was found that the dominant factor is the grain matrix chemistry [49].

item.statement: The authors observed a trade-off where He implantation alone causes grain growth, whereas dual-beam irradiation (heavy ions + He) causes grain refinement, suggesting the heavy ion component is critical for stability.
quotes: However, during the dual-beam irradiation, grain refinement occurred, and the average grain size dropped to 21.1 ± 1.4 nm after a total irradiation time of ~94 mins.
However, grain refinement was not observed for the He only case, but rather grain growth occurred as shown in Fig. 3.
This suggests that such a grain refinement observed in the dual-beam irradiation case was caused by a cascade effect.

item.statement: The authors propose that future work must include response to neutron irradiation to advance the technology readiness level of the material.
quotes: We acknowledge that further work (e.g., response to neutron irradiation) is necessary to advance the technology readiness level (TRL) of this material
and that the effect of composition changes in mechanical strength should be investigated.
Tensile measurements should follow on coarse grain and bulk forms.

item.statement: The authors suggest that the effect of Short-Range Order (SRO) on the mechanical behavior of future RHEAs in extreme environments is a topic to be further explored.
quotes: The effect of SRO on the mechanical behavior of future RHEA in extreme environments is another research topic to be further explored.
It also should be noted that different compositions of this alloy system can have different SRO parameters and different elemental segregation behavior
and therefore, are expected to have different mechanical properties.

item.statement: The study notes that the deconvolution of multiple effects contributing to hardness increase after irradiation depends on complex synergistic processes that are difficult to isolate.

This fact is confirmed when further depths—beyond the zone of influence of Ar irradiation/implantation—are analyzed.

item.statement: The authors state that the specific mechanisms of grain fragmentation during dual-beam irradiation were observed at discrete intervals because the fragmentation process occurred faster than the recording frame rate.
quotes: The in situ nature of the experiments performed in this work has allowed us to observe the grain refinement effect in real-time, albeit the division of some grains into sub-grains was observed at discrete time intervals
since the fragmentation process was occurring at faster time scales than the frame rate used during the data recording.
Figure 8 shows grain fragmentation that occurred during the dual-beam irradiation.
